edition: Coptic SCRIPTORIUM, TEI with word-level annotation. Gospel of Thomas = Nag Hammadi Codex II,2 (Sahidic). Pistis Sophia = Codex Askewianus, complete in four books. Mysteries of John the Evangelist.
license: CC-BY 4.0 — declared in each file's TEI <availability> header, verified per file, not inferred from the repository README
normalization: flat ref-tagged lines: '<Work> <ref>\t<text>' — word tokens rejoined from TEI <w>

scope.held: The Coptic Gnostic material available under an open licence in machine-readable form at this commit.
scope.not_held: Nag Hammadi Codices I and III–XIII. Of the fifty-two tractates, only NHC II,2 is seated. The remaining tractates exist in print editions (Claremont, Brill) and are not available as openly licensed machine-readable Coptic.
scope.ruling: Seated as coptic-gnostic rather than nag-hammadi. The corpus is not the Nag Hammadi library; naming it so would assert a completeness the seat does not have.

declared_absences.work: The Apocryphon of John (the Secret Book of John)
declared_absences.why: The foundational Sethian text, surviving in four manuscripts, and the closest thing Gnosticism has to a canonical scripture. No openly licensed machine-readable Coptic edition exists. Searched 2026-08-21: Coptic SCRIPTORIUM does not hold it; authenticated GitHub search returns one edition whose Coptic derives from scanned PDFs of Meyer 2007 and Linssen, relicensed CC BY-SA by a party that does not hold those rights; Schmidt 1905 is public domain but is the Pistis Sophia volume, and archive.org OCR strips Coptic script entirely; Till 1955, the Berlin Codex edition, remains in copyright.
declared_absences.ruling: Not seated rather than seated defectively. A corpus whose licence is asserted by a party who cannot grant it would place a rights defect inside the sovereign record — the failure this archive exists to document. Absent-and-declared over present-and-defective.
declared_absences.opening: One text, four witnesses. A synoptic open edition of the Apocryphon of John is the narrowest and highest-value gap in the openly licensed Coptic record.

declared_absences.work: Nag Hammadi Codices I and III–XIII
declared_absences.why: Fifty-one of the fifty-two tractates. Print editions only (Claremont, Brill); no open machine-readable Coptic.

declared_absences.work: The Qumran sectarian corpus (Dead Sea Scrolls)
declared_absences.why: Qumran-Digital publishes Open Access with a permissive robots.txt but is JS-rendered with no discoverable text endpoint; the Leon Levy Digital Library returns 403; authenticated GitHub search finds nothing licensed and authoritative. Transcribed decades ago and publicly funded, yet not openly machine-readable.

doctrine: Declared absence follows the DUD doctrine: present-but-presented-as-absent is the archive's worst self-manufactured category. A gap named, dated and reasoned is a finding; a gap papered over is a defect.
